LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 13.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.1: Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 13 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we listen attentively? 2. How can you tell that someone is attentive?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. select words and phrases with the target sounds /m/ /n/ /ŋ/, digraphs and consonant clusters from a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use similes and vocabulary related to the theme correctly in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. select words and phrases with the target sounds /m/ /n/ /ŋ/, digraphs and consonant clusters from a text,

   Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use similes and vocabulary related to the theme correctly in sentences,

   Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a dialogue from an audio-visual recording or read by the teacher and select words with the target sounds, digraphs and clusters,

2. say words containing the sounds /m/ /n/ /ŋ/ with peers, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a dialogue from an audio-visual recording or read by the teacher and select words with the target sounds, digraphs and clusters,
2. say words containing the sounds /m/ /n/ /ŋ/ with peers, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner identifies similes from audio material and constructs

sentences using those similes collaboratively.

• Digital Literacy is achieved as the learner interacts with digital content when listening to dialogues from digital

devices.

102

Values:
Responsibility is developed as learners take up initiative to familiarise themselves with words and expressions like

saving, money and a proverb like: ‘A fool and his money are soon parted’.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial literacy is inculcated as the learner listens to dialogues based on the theme of money.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can apply intensive listening in learning all areas as listening is a key skill for learning.
